newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Summit finds gold intersections at Carrick.
newsitem.headline: Summit finds gold intersections at Carrick.

text.p: Summit Gold NL said on Monday the first assay reverse circulation (RC) percussion drill testing of the Lower Carrick gold arsenic soil anomaly had returned several intersections containing anomalous gold.
Assay results had now been received for the first seven holes drilled along 700 metres of strike.
"All holes, for which results have been received so far, have intersected gold mineralisation within a wide altered shear zone," Summit said in a statement.
A total of over 3,000 metres of drilling is underway on the project which is located on the Carrick Range in Central Otago on New Zealand's South Island.
To date, 15 of the planned 20 or so RC percussion drill holes had been drilled for a total of 2,071 metres of drilling.
"The Carrick drill program is on schedule with the drilling expected to be completed by late May," Summit said.
